headline: GE Vernova Hitachi and Blue Energy have agreed to move to detailed design and licensing of a gas-plus-nuclear power plant near Victoria, Texas, to serve a data center.
score_reason: Lowered from 5 to 3: the announcement was made on 13 Aug 2026 and was published by ANS on 17 Aug, so this is old news, and the plant still needs a 2027 investment decision.
importance_line: Texas power supply for data centers could one day include small nuclear reactors, but the plant is only a plan that depends on a final investment decision in 2027 and on regulatory approval.
summary: The American Nuclear Society's Nuclear Newswire reports that GE Vernova Hitachi Nuclear Energy and Blue Energy announced an agreement to start engineering design, licensing and safety analysis for a possible plant in Victoria, Texas, that pairs gas turbines with small modular reactors, compact nuclear units, subject to a final investment decision in 2027. Blue Energy expects gas turbines to supply about 1 gigawatt to a nearby data center by 2030 and five reactors to add about 1.5 gigawatts of nuclear power from 2032; the announcement dates from 13 Aug 2026.
notes: ANS page is dated 17 Aug 2026 in its own URL; the 'Thursday' of the text is 13 Aug 2026.
